name: Walter Grainger
bio: A servant at the house in High Street, Oxford, where Lord Alfred Douglas had rooms — 'about sixteen when I knew him,' Wilde swore of 1893 — who waited at table during Wilde's stays and asked Wilde to find him a place; Wilde brought him to 'The Cottage' at Goring as under-butler from June-July 1893 until Wilde left in October. Queensberry's plea alleged solicitation and gross indecency at Oxford and Goring; the allegations, outside the Central Criminal Court's jurisdiction, were never charged and Grainger never testified. Carson's pursuit of Wilde's answer to 'Did you ever kiss him?' — 'Oh, dear no. He was a peculiarly plain boy' — is recorded by Hyde as the turning point of the libel trial.
bio_sources: Wilde's libel-trial cross-examination, Hyde, Trials (1948), pp. 150-151 (djvu OCR)
Wilde's final-trial cross-examination, Hyde, Trials (1948), p. 320 (djvu OCR)
Queensberry's plea, Hyde, Trials (1948), pp. 343-344 (IIIF page images 2026-08-03)
Hyde, Trials (1948), Introduction pp. 51-52 (the cross-examination climax; djvu OCR)
bio_note: The age sixteen is Wilde's own sworn estimate at the libel trial, NOT stated in the plea as printed by Hyde (verified in the source image) — the ROSTER's 'aged 16 (plea)' attribution needs adjusting to '(Wilde's testimony)'. The General Index of Complete Letters (2000) has no Grainger entry (verified at the rendered index page, printed p. 1248: the sequence runs 'Grain, J. DATES: NOT FOUND; RECORDED AS UNRECOVERED FROM THE SOURCES CONSULTED. He was a servant at a certain house in High Street, Oxford, where Lord Alfred Douglas had rooms' (Hyde, printed p. 149-150 region; located in the IA OCR text, consistent with the in the source reading already recorded above). McKenna's endnotes cite a 'statement of Walter Grainger, 1895, witness statements, private collection' - a document not in public hands and not consulted. SWEEP FOR DATES, 2026-08-03 (what was searched): the Complete Letters (2000) OCR mirror plus the General Index; McKenna, The Secret Life of Oscar Wilde (2008), repo PDF; Murray, Bosie (2020), repo PDF; Frankel, The Unrepentant Years (2017), repo PDF; Hyde, The Trials of Oscar Wilde, in the Internet Archive copy (item in.ernet.dli.2015.499238, OCR text downloaded and searched, key pages then read as page images); and the open web. No birth or death date is recorded in any source consulted.
